decks.title: Albumin: when to give it
decks.summary: The four indications for short-term albumin, large-volume paracentesis, long-term albumin when a TIPS is not possible, and terlipressin with albumin in HRS-AKI, with what the volume does to the pressures.

decks.title: Ascites: why it forms and how it is treated
decks.summary: How ascites forms in the sinusoids, what diagnostic paracentesis shows, and what each treatment does: large-volume paracentesis with albumin, diuretics and TIPS.

decks.title: Budd–Chiari syndrome, step by step
decks.summary: Budd–Chiari syndrome from diagnosis through the four steps of management (anticoagulation, angioplasty and stenting, TIPS or DIPS, and transplant), the choice of anticoagulant, assessment of response, acute liver failure and HCC surveillance.

decks.title: Carvedilol, from the first visit to stopping
decks.summary: Carvedilol through every stage: why not before CSPH, when to start it, who can forgo screening endoscopy, when to reduce or hold it and when to restart it, EVL after a bleed, a TIPS, and the HVPG that lets it stop.

decks.title: Treating the cause
decks.summary: Four patients whose cause is treated: hepatitis C cured early, hepatitis C cured with CSPH that persists, MASH cirrhosis with weight loss, and alcohol-associated cirrhosis after abstinence. LSM shows whether CSPH has resolved.

decks.title: Choose the treatment
decks.summary: Five cases, one slide each: a variceal bleed, refractory ascites, PVT in cirrhosis, recent PVT without cirrhosis and Budd–Chiari syndrome, each with the choice the guidelines make and why.

decks.title: Portal pressure as a circuit
decks.summary: Portal hypertension as a circuit: increased inflow, increased resistance, collaterals in parallel and TIPS, each interpreted as ΔP = Q × R.

decks.title: The portal circulation
decks.summary: The normal portal circulation, from the splanchnic bed to the right atrium. Ends with the definition of portal hypertension.

decks.title: A day in the portal vein
decks.short: A day in the portal vein
decks.summary: What changes the portal pressure within hours: a meal, a 1 L saline bolus and deep breathing, in one man with CSPH, and why liver stiffness is measured fasting.

decks.title: Doppler of the portal system
decks.summary: What Doppler measures in the portal and hepatic veins, and how to read a waveform in order: direction, velocity, shape. Five cases to interpret before the answer, from hepatofugal portal flow to TIPS stenosis, then a table that compares them.

decks.title: Encephalopathy and shunting
decks.summary: How shunted splanchnic blood reaches the brain: covert HE, a large splenorenal shunt and the consequences of closing it, and the stent diameter and rifaximin that lower the risk of HE after a TIPS.

decks.title: The varix changes when you insufflate
decks.summary: Small and large varices, red wale marks as a separate finding, and what insufflation does to the varix seen at endoscopy and to its transmural pressure.

decks.title: Gastric varices
decks.summary: The Sarin classes, carvedilol before a first bleed, cyanoacrylate and TIPS after one, what BRTO does to the portal pressure, and splenic vein thrombosis: EUS-guided coils and cyanoacrylate for the varix, then splenectomy cures it.

decks.title: HVPG, PPG and EUS-PPG compared
decks.summary: How the HVPG, the EUS-PPG and the PPG are measured, and what each detects in cirrhosis, MASLD, porto-sinusoidal vascular disorder, Budd–Chiari syndrome, right heart failure and after a TIPS.

decks.title: Measuring HVPG and PPG
decks.summary: How the HVPG is measured and interpreted, where it misleads, and when to measure the PPG instead.

decks.title: The circulation in cirrhosis
decks.summary: Why cirrhosis raises the cardiac output and the heart rate and lowers the arterial pressure, how splanchnic vasodilation raises the portal pressure, what a 1 L blood loss does to both, and why overtransfusion raises the portal pressure.

decks.title: The kidney in cirrhosis
decks.summary: Why the abdominal perfusion pressure is the MAP minus the intra-abdominal pressure and not a measure of kidney function, how tense ascites, large-volume paracentesis, carvedilol and hemorrhage change it, and the Baveno VIII steps for HRS-AKI and before a TIPS.

decks.title: Landmark trials, replayed on the model
decks.summary: The trials behind beta-blockers in CSPH, restrictive transfusion, early TIPS, TIPS for recurrent ascites and rifaximin before a TIPS, in the order a patient meets them. For each, who was enrolled, the treatment on the model, and what the trial found.

decks.title: Inside the lobule: the site of each disease
decks.summary: The lobule from portal tract to central vein, and the point in it where each disease adds resistance. Ends with what the wedged pressure reflects at each site.

decks.title: MASLD and portal hypertension
decks.summary: MASLD cirrhosis with obesity, where part of the resistance is presinusoidal and the HVPG underestimates the portal pressure gradient: what to measure, how a BMI ≥30 changes the liver stiffness rule, what weight loss may do, and which drugs and alcohol advice apply.

decks.title: Children with portal vein thrombosis
decks.summary: A child with chronic PVT: cavernous transformation, the normal HVPG and high PPG, liver and spleen stiffness that cannot be relied on alone, the meso-Rex bypass and its effect on hepatic blood flow, and the distal splenorenal shunt (DSRS) when a bypass is not feasible.

decks.title: Presinusoidal portal hypertension
decks.summary: Schistosomiasis and porto-sinusoidal vascular disorder (PSVD): varices and splenomegaly with normal liver stiffness and a normal HVPG, because the resistance is in the portal tracts.

decks.title: Preventing the next variceal bleed
decks.summary: After a first variceal bleed: why EVL alone lets varices recur, how carvedilol lowers the portal pressure behind them, why the two together are first-line, and the TIPS that follows when they fail.

decks.title: After the sinusoids: central veins and the heart
decks.summary: Sinusoidal obstruction syndrome, heart failure, constrictive pericarditis and an IVC web: hepatic venous outflow obstruction, and what hepatic venous catheterization and Doppler show in each.

decks.title: Cirrhosis in pregnancy
decks.summary: One woman with compensated cirrhosis through pregnancy: increased blood volume and portal inflow, enlarging varices, second-trimester EGD, band ligation and propranolol, and delivery.

decks.title: Portal vein thrombosis
decks.summary: Prehepatic resistance from PVT: acute thrombosis on Doppler, the normal HVPG and high PPG, cavernous transformation months later, and partial PVT in cirrhosis from diagnosis to 6 months of anticoagulation.

decks.title: Decompensation and recompensation
decks.summary: One patient over two years: CSPH, the first ascites, diuretics, then removal of the cause and recompensation. The portal pressure falls, but recompensation is not a cure.

decks.title: Same gradient, different patient
decks.summary: Four patients with the same HVPG and different PPGs, portal flow and collaterals: what the wedged pressure leaves out, and what to read beside it.

decks.title: TIPS and shunts
decks.summary: Spontaneous portosystemic shunts, TIPS indications and the pre-TIPS evaluation, the effects of the stent on portal pressure, hepatic perfusion and the heart, stent diameter, and the distal splenorenal shunt (DSRS). Ends with a comparison of gradient, sinusoidal flow and hepatic encephalopathy risk.

decks.title: Sites and causes of portal hypertension
decks.summary: Six levels of resistance, each with its pressure profile from the splanchnic veins to the right atrium and its HVPG. Ends with a comparison table.

decks.title: Stiffness, platelets and the first visit
decks.summary: LSM by VCTE, spleen size and the platelet count against the portal pressure gradient, then five compensated patients at a first visit: the Baveno VIII LSM and platelet zones, the indeterminate zone, screening endoscopy, carvedilol, and the patients the rules do not fit.

decks.title: One patient, ten years
decks.summary: One man with cirrhosis over ten years: the tests that find CSPH and carvedilol at once, the first ascites, diuretics and a transplant referral, a variceal bleed and banding, rebleeding and TIPS, hepatic encephalopathy, and the transplant evaluation, with a decision at each step.

decks.title: What precipitates decompensation in compensated cirrhosis
decks.summary: A man with CSPH can stay compensated for years, until a second hit precipitates decompensation: a liver injury, an infection or surgery. What each does, what dental care may prevent, and why no long-term antibiotic is started after the first decompensation only to prevent the next.

decks.title: Who should get a TIPS
decks.summary: Seven patients, one decision each: a bleed that qualifies and one that does not, a rebleed, ascites that returns, a failing liver, a congested heart, a past episode of encephalopathy, and an older, frail patient. Ends on a table of what the stent did and what was decided.

decks.title: TIPS: indication to follow-up
decks.summary: TIPS from the indication to the follow-up: preemptive, rescue, salvage and elective stents, who should be prepared or turned away, the placement and the PPG after it, the width, encephalopathy and its reduction, the follow-up Doppler, a stent that narrows, the DIPS and TIPS against BRTO. Ends on a table of what each state does to the PPG and the liver.

decks.title: Doppler ultrasound of TIPS
decks.summary: TIPS Doppler: the pre-TIPS baseline, a patent stent, aliasing, and a stenosed stent with its velocity jet, with the vessels colored by velocity and direction.

decks.title: Lowering portal pressure
decks.summary: Propranolol, carvedilol, octreotide, terlipressin and TIPS in one patient with decompensated cirrhosis, the HVPG fall with each, and a patient with schistosomiasis whose resistance is presinusoidal, where carvedilol adds little.

decks.title: Dual blood supply of the liver
decks.summary: The portal vein and the hepatic artery share hepatic blood flow. The artery buffers every fall in portal flow, after portal vein thrombosis, after TIPS or in cirrhosis; nothing buffers a fall in arterial flow.

decks.title: Two lesions, one circulation
decks.summary: One man with cirrhosis and CSPH gets an occlusive portal vein clot, then constrictive pericarditis, then loses each lesion in turn. The clot raises the PPG and lowers the HVPG, congestion lowers both gradients, and together they pull the HVPG well under the CSPH line and leave the PPG where it began.

decks.title: Resuscitating an acute variceal bleed
decks.summary: One acute variceal bleed from rupture to TIPS: early shock with a normal hemoglobin, octreotide and volume before endoscopy, restrictive transfusion, band ligation and a preemptive TIPS; then rebleeding by day 5, the stent or balloon bridge, and the rescue TIPS.

decks.title: Collaterals and varices
decks.summary: Six months of progression, then the esophageal varices, carvedilol at CSPH, and the other collateral routes. Ends with why heart failure rarely causes varices.

decks.title: Where is the resistance?
decks.summary: Six unnamed patients. Read each case and its pressure ladder and locate the resistance; one tap then shows where the pressure is lost.
